title: Anyone up to run? Looking for testers
author: Alessioga

comments.author: Alessioga
comments.body:
**What model?** Opus 5 for almost all of it — coding, debugging, the look passes. Fable 5.1 for planning. About 31 sessions over two and a half weeks.

**How does Claude run Unity?** Desktop app, no MCP and no Unity plugin. It runs terminal commands and edits files directly. Unity can be driven from the command line, so Claude wrote a set of C# editor scripts it then calls itself — build the game, run the tests, render a frame. That last one matters: it can screenshot the game and look at what it just made, instead of me being the only pair of eyes.

**How do you make assets?** This is where it differs from most "I built a game with AI" posts: **there's no 3D pipeline at all.** No Blender, no Meshy, not a single imported model in the project. Every board, rider, wall and texture is generated by C# at runtime.

The only generated art is 2D and it's all menus — the wordmark and the illustration plates, via gpt-image-2. Music and sound effects are ElevenLabs.

**How do you keep it consistent?** One house style block, appended word for word to every image prompt — line weight, flat fills, the exact palette, what's forbidden. It's checked into the repo next to the prompts.

One warning: don't use Gemini for anything needing a transparent background. Ask for one and it returns a JPEG — no alpha channel — with a *picture of* a transparency checkerboard painted in. Looks right as a thumbnail, composites onto your UI as a grey grid.

**Cost?** $**/month Claude, $**/month ElevenLabs, image generation metered at about $\_\_.

**What's the gameplay?** A racer with no grip. You stand on a thruster board in a city's storm drains, each thumbstick driving one side, everything running off one finite energy core — so steering literally costs you top speed, and if you run it dry you become a projectile. Ten circuits, storm drain up to a glass tube in orbit.

**Can I play it?** Yes, both free. iPhone/iPad: 0n1studios.com/runoff/testflight. Android: 0n1studios.com/runoff/testers — that one's a closed test and it has never run on a real Android phone, so I want the ugly bug reports.

Happy to answer anything.
